### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/indexing.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via keyParts (symbol, a field of interface SchemaSyncIndexStep), rowScope (symbol, a field of interface SchemaSyncIndexStep), create_table (literal, a string literal in collectSchemaSyncIndexes), os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/index.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via MetadataProtocol (symbol, a top-level type), os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via MetadataProtocol (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataProtocol (symbol, a top-level type), os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via os migrate plan (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 958734cbac39a6d64aa6b3a3eba3f776a87eec5b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d7c8a211cec59ef1942d2606144f402cea865d4` — the merge of head `4627b55082d1ae544878c7dcbfa7febcb6db6710` into base `958734cbac39a6d64aa6b3a3eba3f776a87eec5b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d7c8a211cec59ef1942d2606144f402cea865d4 && git checkout 7d7c8a211cec59ef1942d2606144f402cea865d4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 958734cbac39a6d64aa6b3a3eba3f776a87eec5b 4627b55082d1ae544878c7dcbfa7febcb6db6710 && git checkout -B drift-repro 958734cbac39a6d64aa6b3a3eba3f776a87eec5b && git merge --no-ff 4627b55082d1ae544878c7dcbfa7febcb6db6710

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 958734cbac39a6d64aa6b3a3eba3f776a87eec5b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 958734cbac39a6d64aa6b3a3eba3f776a87eec5b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `be36fbc9438d9c2fe02efc2acdd19047fefd31a6`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone. The committed tree touches no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path: `check-governed-merges` on the file list reads NOT governed.
- The widening has two parts. ⑴ `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (published, no `private`) re-exports `buildUserPermissionSetPackagelessIndexPresenceSql` from `src/index.ts`. It is the guard build's own catalog statement, so the plan asks the owner instead of keeping a second spelling. ⑵ `os migrate plan --json` (`@objectstack/cli`, published) gains the always-present array `schemaSyncIndexes`. Its entries are `{ migration, table, index, keyParts, rowScope, status: build|blocked|unreadable, onCreatedTable?, duplicateKeys?, duplicateRows?, detail? }`, and they are never counted in `total`. Nothing accepted before is refused. No spec contract declares the plan's JSON shape (0 hits for its sibling keys `nullableTenantColumns` / `unmanagedTables` under `packages/spec/src/**`). `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` documents the new key in the same PR.
- The card's mechanism premise was corrected by measurement and recorded in the PR body. The plan listed no runtime-owned index at all, and the activation-ledger guard is built at `kernel:ready` behind `runPlatformMigrations`, which one-shot CLI boots turn off, so `apply` never builds it. Keeping it out of the plan matches the 2026-08-22 ruling recorded in `runtime-index-preflight.ts`, and a pin holds that split.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for both packages: `Metadata-protocol: none` (maintainer ruling A on #25105, the level follows the metadata protocol alone). The changeset and the PR body both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The dev ran `check-changeset-no-major` against that body at this head and it exited 0.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No security, permission or tenancy boundary moves: the new code path is read-only (catalog presence and duplicate probe) and writes nothing.
- The PR is authored as `objectstack-fleet[bot]` through the relay.
- Outside the claimed surface: a new sibling util `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-sync-indexes.ts` (in place of growing `schema-migrate.ts`), and the one-line re-export in `metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`. Both are named in the PR body. The fenced `user-permission-set-packageless-index.ts` is untouched.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32460-migrate-plan-permset-guard`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSZ51q2s3nMfakhdJ3`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-12T09:22Z

Head-sha: `be36fbc9438d9c2fe02efc2acdd19047fefd31a6` · card #32460 · claim 6816688987 (amended on the card) · report 6819648862 · contract review PASS 6819743219

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, first line `Fixes #32460`, no other card number beside a closing keyword. Not governed, 626 changed lines (+616 / −10), under 3000. Both published packages touched (`@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`) carry a `patch` changeset. No `content/docs/releases/` change.
- **Premise:** the card's ask holds (the plan was silent about a DDL that apply runs). Its "as it lists the other runtime-owned indexes" was measured false: the plan listed none, and the activation-ledger guard is not apply's work. The dev followed the measurement and recorded it in the PR body. The seat re-read `plan.ts` on `origin/main`: 0 hits for either guard name.
- **Declaration corrected in patch round 1:** `Clause-②: no` → `yes (widening)` (a new published export, plus the new `--json` key `schemaSyncIndexes`; precedent #30887 6731543957). The changeset was fixed by the dev at `be36fbc9`, and the PR body line was rewritten by the seat (read back identical). `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` are unchanged.
- **Pins:** 12 new unit cases and 2 integration cases on the real grant-guard harness. The ablation of the presence check turns exactly the 2 "present gives no step" pins red. A run through the public door (`os serve` provision, drop the guard, then `migrate plan` in both faces) shows the line and the JSON entry.
- **Accepted deviations:** the logic lives in a new sibling util, and `metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` gains one re-export (producer side, so there is a single spelling). Fixture triage in `plan.apply-limit.test.ts`: the `--json` key sets gain the new key. Sentences checked against the diff: the changeset bullets ("A guard that already stands is no step … a plan with nothing to apply … A Turso remote primary's plan lists none") and the `cli.mdx` sentence "Under `--json` the section is the `schemaSyncIndexes` array". Both match `collectSchemaSyncIndexes`.
- **Out of scope, filed:** apply's own pre-prompt listing omits the same guard. That is filed as #32653 (class b, `Blocked-by: #32460`). The other notes stay in the PR's Acceptance notes.
- **Not measured locally:** 3 derived gates (exit 3, prerequisite) and `check:type-check-debt` at the merged head. CI's check-runs on this head are the reading of record before landing.
- **Landing:** readying and auto-merge happen once every check on `be36fbc9` is green or an expected skip.
